payload.conclusion: DRAFT prepared by AI from explicit text only — not verified by a scholar. Annual assessment: at the khums year end, one-fifth of the income from work, business, salaries and rents that exceeds the expenses of oneself and one's dependants («احکام خمس», income chapter). Gifts and other payments one could not claim are not liable; inheritance is not liable. Costs of earning are deducted; a business debt only from the income it produced; debts for this year's living needs that arose after the year's first income are deducted without being paid. Tax is mu'nah: tax for this year's earnings is deducted; past years' tax paid this year is deducted only if it relates to this year (tax section). Paying khums before the year end is allowed (Q227); khums of last year paid from this year's income is not deducted (khums is also due on what was paid, Q247). Wages owed and collectable at the year end are liable even if not received; if not collectable they are income of the year received (receivables sections); credit sales need the cash price and the mark-up separately (review). Bringing the year forward is allowed; postponing is not (assess at the current date first), so a period longer than a year stops for review (Q234, Q235). Separate jobs with separate accounts have separate years without offsetting (Q245); how living expenses are borne across them is not stated (review). Spending on needs, and needs debts of this or past years, paid from this year's income within five days after the year end are deducted (debts and savings sections, Q271). A rise caused by inflation is not a gain: sale gains, deposit profit and the growth of working capital and shares held for growth are liable only above the taxed value or principal plus inflation, using the person's own inflation figure (inflation, added-value, bank-profit, capital and shares sections); mu'nah and gifts not held for trade owe nothing on sale. Savings are liable, except savings for marriage once steps began, emergency savings that would not suffice after khums, and the last salary that would not cover the next month after khums; savings for near-future necessities are not quantified (review). Mahr and diyah received are not liable (mahr and diyah sections). Insurance premiums from the year's income are mu'nah; investment-type payments are liable each year end (premiums section). Insurance compensation paid to the insured is earned income; life-insurance payouts to the spouse and children, and payments to a non-party, are not liable (payouts section).
payload.explanation: Encoded as one Rule Builder rule (annual surplus). Counted: salary, business, freelance and rental income, pensions (liable like salary); bonuses only if contractually owed («کارانه»; festive bonus and reward are not liable). Not counted: gifts, inheritance and charity or support received (the gifts chapter: payments one could not claim). A survivors' pension is not liable (Q223). Costs of earning (and business debts) reduce only business, freelance and rental income. Living expenses are deducted unless paid from income whose year had passed (that money owes khums on the purchase price with inflation) or spent before the year's first income (balance chapter); spending beyond status or extravagant stops for review (only the excess is liable). Debts for living needs are deducted only when they arose this year after the first income and are unpaid. Separate lines of work with separate accounts where one made a loss stop for review (the several-jobs note: losses are not offset). Investment returns and sale proceeds stop as uncovered entries. Holdings at year end: things bought with this year's income and still held are counted at their year-end value, and the price paid is deducted; household items needed and kept available are exempt even if unused; capital whose khums would leave too little (or doubtfully enough) for living is exempt; land or an unfinished home for needed housing is exempt (chapters on items beyond mu'nah, capital, capital without khums, shares, gradual acquisition). Decision 81 (form): valuation by how an item was paid for (Tables 1–2), loan-bought items counted at the part repaid, mixed exempt money (note 11), items used for both life and work (note 22), waqf (note 10), dowry (notes 7–8), Hajj savings (note 19), provident fund, gratuity and leave encashment (note 9), partnership (note 5), loans given (note 29), animals, crops and stock at the khums date (Table 3, notes 27–28), and the form's exemptions.
conditions: At the khums year end, exceeding the year's expenses
Debts: for this year's needs, arising after the year's first income
Business debts: only against the income they produced
exceptions: Gifts and payments one could not claim
